Method of Attack: Outlook sends an email in both encrypted and unencrypted form causing leak of S/MIME encrypted emails
Leak occurs when sending emails in plaintext or responding to plaintext emails with encryption
Leak occurs with SMTP servers and Exchange infrastructure with TLS disabled
Leak allows attacker to read encrypted email content by snooping traffic or accessing email previews without private key
Indicators of Compromise: Emails encrypted with S/MIME standard leaked
Leak occurs only for emails sent using Outlook
Leak occurs only one server hop for Exchange infrastructure with TLS disabled
